producer_report.summary: `athena status` now reports, for each reading rule, how many first readings it refused and how many second readings it refused, over the last 50 first readings. The Hestia sweep flags any rule that refused more than 30% of those first readings. Root cause: nothing recorded which rule refused a reading. `read_once` held the refusal only in memory, and a double refusal left no Reading record. The fix records it where it arises. Each reader invocation whose output reached the rules now carries an optional `reading_attempt` field. It holds the attempt number (1 or 2) and, when refused, `{rule, text}`. The rule name comes from `refusing_check`, the same gate the refusal corpus pins. A size refusal is named `check_reading_size`, and other invalid reader output is `other`. The stored text is redacted. Status adds `ReadingRuleStats::compute` with `READING_WINDOW` = 50. It takes the newest 50 first readings by `started_at`, pairs each with its re-read at seq+1, and counts per rule. It also keeps the most common first-refusal text, with ties going to the most recent. The sweep adds the check `reading-rule-refusals` (`REFUSAL_FLAG_PERCENT` = 30, `MIN_FIRST_READINGS` = 10, flag when `first_refused * 100 > first_readings * 30`). It runs only in `hestia_sweep_with`, so `hestia_sweep`, `default_checks()` and the 3-ui-line test are unchanged. Below 10 first readings, or with no recorded attempts, it examines 0 and flags nothing, and no "healthy" text exists. No reading rule, refusal text, prompt or governance file changed. Departures from the brief: the window is the 50 newest first readings, not 50 jobs, because a double refusal leaves no Reading and would otherwise be hidden. A second refusal is counted under the rule that refused the re-read. A rule is shown only if it refused at least once.

A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixture reading records where rule A refuses 3 first readings and 1 second reading, and rule B refuses 1 first reading. It asserts that the status output reports, per rule, the first-refusal count and the second-refusal count, over at most the last 50 readings.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the status/hestia fixture helpers live in `status::reading_rule_tests`, and the hestia tests reuse them.

Because the gate stops at the first refusing check, a later rule in the order is hidden whenever an earlier one refuses the same reading, so its rate can be understated. This is documented in the `ReadingRuleStats` doc comment and in the CHANGELOG.
Records written before this change have no `reading_attempt`, so the window starts empty. Below 10 first readings the sweep stays silent.
Refusal texts name request-specific paths, so exact-text grouping often ties at 1 and the 'most common text' is then the most recent example. The finding shows its count.
mistakes: I first made `ReadError::Refused` carry the rule too, which left the field unread (a dead-code warning). I reverted it, because the rule is already stored in the invocation record.
clippy rejected the nested map type in `ReadingRuleStats::compute` as too complex. I added the `RuleRow` type alias.
learnings: `refusing_check` in reading/checks.rs returns the name of the first refusing check, so the rule name needed no second list of names.

The live invocation file written by `invoke_and_record` is a state-directory mirror. The committed record is the one `read_once` returns, so `reading_attempt` set after that call reaches the committed record, and run_pin_tests confirms it.
`Records::jobs` holds `JobRecords.invocations` for every job, which gave a direct source for the per-reading data.

Hestia tests pin `default_checks()` empty, two checks in a `hestia_sweep` record, and exactly 3 ui lines per `hestia_sweep_with`. The new check therefore runs only in `hestia_sweep_with` and prints no line.
desires: Read access to the saved output of a large tool result, so a full-suite run did not need repeating.
